newsitem.title: USA: Ohio $5 bln school funding plan may include bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ohio $5 bln school funding plan may include bonds.

text.p: A plan to raise about $5 billion over five years to mainly fund school infrastructure projects in Ohio may include state bonds, a key legislative backer of the plan said Tuesday.

State Rep. William Batchelder, R-Medina, said that while the group of 15 Republican House members backing the plan is split on whether to use bonds, he believes issuing general obligation bonds for the program was the way to go.
Batchelder said that if bonds are included in the program, lawmakers would have to place a proposed constitutional amendment on the November ballot to allow for the GO bond issuance.
Legislation is expected to be drafted in the next two weeks, he added.
The Republican lawmakers' plan unveiled Tuesday already calls for a referendum on a five-year, one percent sales tax increase that would raise an average of $1 billion a year.

Revenues from the tax increase, which would become effective Jan. 1, 1998, would be distributed to schools, with $3.75 billion slated for infrastructure assistance, $1 billion for technology improvements and $250 million for instructional materials, according to a fact sheet on the plan.

Schools would be required to raise matching funds in order to receive the state revenues. The percentage of those matching funds would range from five percent to 50 percent depending on the financial condition of the school district.
The lawmakers estimated the local match for the infrastructure program to total nearly $1.3 billion.
Batchelder said he expected most of the school districts would have to issue bonds to raise the the matching funds.
